whoIsThisFor.heading: Who should take the Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional exam?

personas.label: Consumer goods implementation consultants
personas.description: You configure retail execution solutions for consumer goods manufacturers or distributors and want to show that you understand their field workflows.

personas.label: Salesforce administrators in consumer goods
personas.description: You support a Consumer Goods Cloud org and need to understand how visits, store checks, and field teams are set up.

personas.label: Retail execution and field sales partners
personas.description: You design tools for representatives who visit stores, check shelves, and capture orders, and want to validate your configuration knowledge.

examDifficulty.heading: How difficult is the Consumer Goods Cloud AP exam?
examDifficulty.summary: The exam focuses on field work for consumer goods companies, including visit planning, store execution, direct store delivery, and performance reporting. Candidates new to retail operations may need time to learn the terms and how the activities connect.
bullets: 33 scored questions in 60 minutes, plus up to five unscored questions that do not count.
64% to pass, which is 22 correct answers out of 33.
Store visits and execution: Review visit plans, routes, shelf checks, surveys, and the data reps capture in stores.
Orders and inventory: Understand direct store delivery, pricing, and stock held in delivery vehicles.
examDifficulty.passRateGuidance: Practice tracing a store visit from planning through data capture and follow-up. Aim to score at least 75% on practice sets and explain why each step or feature fits the workflow. Hands-on work with Consumer Goods Cloud is useful preparation.

examFormat.heading: Consumer Goods Cloud Accredited Professional exam format
examFormat.intro: The exam is proctored online or at a test center. Questions ask how Consumer Goods Cloud supports retail field work.
examFormat.scenarioPercent: Some questions describe a task such as scheduling a store call, checking shelf compliance, or capturing a delivery order. Identify the record, rule, or workflow that supports that task.
bestWayToPass: Plan visits: Learn how visit plans, templates, routes, and store priorities shape a representative's schedule.
Capture store results: Review surveys, shelf checks, photos, and the information a rep records during a visit.
Follow delivery orders: Understand how field orders, pricing, promotions, invoicing, and vehicle stock fit together.
Use performance measures: Know what visit completion, on-shelf availability, and compliance measures tell a field manager.

certificationCard.description: This exam covers Consumer Goods Cloud setup for consumer goods manufacturers and distributors, including store visits, retail execution, in-store checks, direct store delivery, and field performance. The guide allows up to five additional unscored questions. The exam is 33 scored questions in 60 minutes, with a 64% pass mark, weighted towards Data Setup and Visit Execution (36% each).

keyConcepts.h2: Consumer Goods Cloud AP: concepts to review

blocks.heading: Visit Planning and Routes
blocks.body: Visit plans organize which outlets representatives should call on, how often they should visit, and what they should do there. Route tools help arrange those calls into a workable sequence. Visit templates can provide a consistent set of activities for a type of store. The exam may ask how a plan is assigned to a field team or how priorities affect scheduling.

blocks.heading: Store Visits and Retail Checks
blocks.body: During a visit, a representative can complete assigned activities, answer survey questions, record product availability, and attach photos. These records give managers evidence of what happened in the store. Image recognition can help interpret shelf photos where it is configured. Learn how visit tasks and assessments capture information that can be reviewed later.

blocks.heading: Direct Store Delivery and Inventory
blocks.body: In direct store delivery, a field representative may take an order and fulfill it from a delivery vehicle. The process can include building a cart, confirming the order, preparing an invoice, taking payment, and updating stock. Prices and promotions affect the order, while inventory records help track what remains in the vehicle. Be able to follow the process from order capture to completion.

blocks.heading: Retail Accounts and Assortments
blocks.body: Retail accounts represent individual outlets, chains, or distributors. Store attributes and account relationships help teams group outlets and plan appropriate activity. Assortments describe products intended for a store or group of stores, while planograms describe how products should be arranged on shelves. Understand how these records support account planning and store execution.

blocks.heading: Field Performance and Analytics
blocks.body: Reports help managers review call completion, product availability, shelf compliance, and promotional results. A useful measure should match the question being asked: completed visits show field activity, while sales lift compares results with a baseline. CRM Analytics can combine field data for broader analysis when configured. Know what each measure tells a manager and what it cannot prove by itself.

scenarioTips.h2: How to prepare for the Consumer Goods Cloud AP exam
scenarioTips.intro: When a question describes a store or field task, identify where it belongs: visit planning, in-store capture, order fulfillment, or reporting. Then select the record or feature that performs that job.

blocks.heading: Understand the Consumer Goods Records
blocks.body: Review how retail stores, accounts, products, visits, assessments, and planograms relate. Use the relationships to determine where a task or result should be recorded.

blocks.heading: Plan Calls by Outlet
blocks.body: Know how teams schedule visits based on store needs and frequency. A visit plan organizes intended calls; route planning helps sequence them for the representative.

blocks.heading: Capture Store Evidence
blocks.body: Understand how activities and surveys collect results during a visit. Shelf data and photos document execution, while reports summarize the captured information.

blocks.heading: Review Shelf Recognition Carefully
blocks.body: Image recognition can analyze shelf photos where the capability is configured. Distinguish the observed shelf from the planogram that describes the intended arrangement.

blocks.heading: Match Metrics to Questions
blocks.body: Use visit completion to assess whether planned calls occurred. Use availability and compliance measures to assess store conditions, and compare sales with a baseline to estimate promotional lift.

nextCertsAfter.heading: Certifications to consider after Consumer Goods Cloud AP
nextCertsAfter.intro: After this credential, you may want to build broader Salesforce skills or specialize in a related role.

sampleQuestions.question: A representative has calls scheduled in stores where mobile coverage is unreliable. Which setup lets them use the call plan while offline?
options: A browser tab kept open all day on the device
A printed route that must be entered again later
The offline-capable mobile app
A daily email with the route attached
sampleQuestions.explanation: The offline-capable mobile app can make assigned work available when the device has no connection.
whyWrong: An open browser session does not by itself provide offline access to the call plan.
A paper route requires manual re-entry and does not capture work in the app.
Email can share a route but does not provide the app's offline workflow.

sampleQuestions.question: In Consumer Goods Cloud, what does a visit record represent?
options: A promotion discount agreed with a retailer
Inventory held at a distribution center
An invoice for goods delivered to the retailer
A planned or completed call at an outlet
sampleQuestions.explanation: A visit represents a field call at an outlet, whether the call is planned or has already taken place.
whyWrong: A promotion stores commercial terms, rather than a representative's store call.
Distribution center inventory is a stock record, not an outlet visit.
An invoice records a financial transaction, not the field activity.

sampleQuestions.question: During one store call, a representative must check stock, photograph a shelf, and place an order. How should those activities be organized?
options: As three separate calls to the same outlet
As three support cases for another team
As tasks associated with the visit
As one free-text note entered after the work is done
sampleQuestions.explanation: Visit tasks keep the required activities together under the store call and its results.
whyWrong: Creating separate calls would fragment work that happens during one visit.
Cases track issues that need support; they are not the normal container for visit activities.
A note alone does not structure the individual checks or order work.

sampleQuestions.question: What does a planogram describe?
options: The intended arrangement of products on a shelf
The retailer's complete order history
The delivery routes used in a region
The payment terms agreed with a retailer
sampleQuestions.explanation: A planogram describes the target shelf layout, which can be compared with what a representative observes.
whyWrong: Order history shows transactions, not where products should appear on a shelf.
Delivery routes plan transportation and do not specify shelf placement.
Payment terms cover finance rather than merchandising layout.

sampleQuestions.question: A representative takes a shelf photo and the system identifies visible products. What capability is being used?
options: A manual count entered by the representative
Image recognition for a shelf audit
An automatic replenishment order to the distribution center
A retailer-provided planogram template
sampleQuestions.explanation: Image recognition analyzes the photo to identify products or shelf conditions for the audit.
whyWrong: Manual counting relies on the rep to enter each observation rather than analyzing the image.
Replenishment may follow an audit but is not the image analysis itself.
A planogram describes the intended layout; it does not identify products in a photo.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a consumer goods team measure its share of shelf?
options: Retailers must publish the figure each quarter
It sets the supplier's payment terms
It determines the approved field headcount
Shelf space can influence what shoppers buy
sampleQuestions.explanation: The amount and placement of shelf space can affect product visibility and sales, so teams track it as an execution measure.
whyWrong: There is no general rule requiring retailers to publish this figure quarterly.
Payment terms are negotiated separately from shelf placement.
Staffing levels are an internal decision, not calculated from shelf share alone.

sampleQuestions.question: A six-week promotion ran in 300 outlets. Which measure best estimates whether it increased sales?
options: The number of display units shipped to stores
The number of photos uploaded by representatives
The number of outlets visited during the promotion
Sales lift compared with a suitable baseline period
sampleQuestions.explanation: Comparing sales with a comparable baseline helps estimate the change associated with the promotion.
whyWrong: Shipments measure product sent to stores, not the resulting sales lift.
Photo counts show data capture volume, not the promotion's sales effect.
Visit counts measure field activity rather than customer purchasing.

sampleQuestions.question: What does trade promotion management help a company do?
options: Recruit and schedule field representatives
Plan and fund promotions with retail partners
Design product packaging artwork
Route delivery vehicles to stores
sampleQuestions.explanation: Trade promotion management supports planning, funding, and tracking promotional activity with retailers.
whyWrong: Recruitment and staffing are workforce activities, not trade promotion planning.
Packaging design is separate from managing retailer promotions.
Vehicle routing is a logistics task rather than promotion management.

sampleQuestions.question: A product is missing from the shelf, but the store has plenty of it in the back room. What problem should the visit record flag?
options: A planogram design error
An in-store replenishment issue
A pricing dispute with the retailer
A shortage at the manufacturer's plant
sampleQuestions.explanation: Because stock is already in the store, moving it from the back room to the shelf is an in-store replenishment issue.
whyWrong: The observation does not show that the intended shelf layout is wrong.
Price does not explain why available stock remains in the back room.
The stock is present at the outlet, so a factory shortage is not indicated.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a company schedule high-volume outlets more often than small stores?
options: Representatives are contractually capped at one call per store
All stores in a chain must be visited on the same day
The mobile app limits the number of weekly calls
Outlet size and sales potential vary
sampleQuestions.explanation: Visit frequency can reflect outlet value and service needs, so a high-volume store may warrant more frequent attention.
whyWrong: This is not generally determined by a fixed contractual limit on calls.
A chain does not need every store visited on the same day.
App synchronization capacity is not the reason to vary call frequency.

sampleQuestions.question: What is one benefit of recording competitor presence during a store visit?
options: It shows how the wider category is performing
It fulfills a universal retailer reporting requirement
It makes measuring the company's own shelf presence unnecessary
It lets the supplier set competitors' retail prices
sampleQuestions.explanation: Competitor observations help put a company's own shelf and sales results in the context of the wider category.
whyWrong: There is no universal requirement for suppliers to report every brand in a store.
Competitor information adds context but does not replace measuring the company's products.
A supplier cannot set another company's prices at a retailer.

sampleQuestions.question: A manager wants to know whether representatives completed their scheduled calls. What should they review?
options: Visit completion compared with the call plan
Product volume shipped into the region
The number of territory photos uploaded
The number of promotions agreed during the quarter
sampleQuestions.explanation: Comparing completed visits with the plan directly shows whether scheduled calls took place.
whyWrong: Shipment volume measures product movement, not completion of store calls.
Photo counts can vary and do not establish whether planned calls happened.
Promotion count measures commercial agreements, not field-call completion.

sampleQuestions.question: A representative captures visit information offline and later reconnects. What should happen to the saved data?
options: It waits for an administrator to approve each upload
It syncs to the org when connectivity returns
It is discarded because offline data cannot be trusted
It is emailed to a manager for manual entry
sampleQuestions.explanation: Offline capture preserves the representative's work so it can synchronize to the org after connectivity returns.
whyWrong: Requiring manual approval for every upload is not the normal offline-sync process.
Offline capture is designed to retain valid work made without a connection.
Email and re-entry would defeat the purpose of capturing information in the app.

sampleQuestions.question: Why might a field team record the price displayed on a store shelf?
options: Suppliers are legally required to enforce each retailer's price
It is the only way to know what the retailer ordered
Shelf price can affect demand and how shoppers view the brand
It sets the representative's commission
sampleQuestions.explanation: The displayed retail price can influence shopper choices and brand positioning, so observing it is useful context.
whyWrong: A supplier generally does not control the retailer's resale price.
Order records show what the retailer purchased; shelf price is a separate observation.
Representative commission is not normally set by the shelf price alone.

sampleQuestions.question: Which statement best describes Consumer Goods Cloud?
options: It plans next year's product portfolio
It schedules factory production
It supports field execution at retail outlets
It manages field staff payroll and expenses
sampleQuestions.explanation: Consumer Goods Cloud supports retail field work such as planning visits, recording store conditions, and managing execution.
whyWrong: Product portfolio planning is a separate business planning activity.
Factory scheduling belongs to manufacturing operations.
Payroll and expenses are handled through workforce or finance systems.
